scope_of_generality_decision.rationale: One public GitHub and Git case can lock conceptual boundaries but cannot validate private, enterprise, non-Git, other-provider, alternate-ID, or arbitrary-history support.
scope_of_generality_decision.title: Case-calibrated generality limit

canonical_case_example.description: The retained Issue observation contains a usable GraphQL node ID.

controlled_vocabulary.meaning: The inspected representation contains a usable value.
controlled_vocabulary.permitted_later_resolution: A later observation may differ or conflict, but this observation remains present in history.
controlled_vocabulary.required_evidence: A bounded inspected representation and the exact field value.

canonical_case_example.description: Issue timeline source index 17 explicitly reports a null actor field in the supplemental observation.

controlled_vocabulary.meaning: The inspected representation explicitly contains null.
controlled_vocabulary.permitted_later_resolution: A later observation may contain a value, but the earlier explicit null remains recorded.
controlled_vocabulary.required_evidence: A bounded inspected representation in which the field is present with null.

canonical_case_example.description: The pre-merge PR representation omits merge_commit_sha and records that field as missing.

controlled_vocabulary.meaning: The inspected representation does not contain the field.
controlled_vocabulary.permitted_later_resolution: A later representation may present or explicitly null the field without rewriting the earlier omission.
controlled_vocabulary.required_evidence: A bounded inspected representation and proof that the field is absent from it.

canonical_case_example.description: The deleted PR-head repository is known as a subject, but no repository representation was obtained.

controlled_vocabulary.meaning: The object or representation is known, but no representation was obtained.
controlled_vocabulary.permitted_later_resolution: A later acquisition may obtain a representation; the earlier unavailable observation remains.
controlled_vocabulary.required_evidence: Evidence that the subject or representation is known plus a bounded acquisition outcome showing none was obtained.

canonical_case_example.description: No access denial was observed; private and permission-hidden records remain unknown and must not be relabeled inaccessible.

controlled_vocabulary.meaning: Access was denied or required authorization that was unavailable.
controlled_vocabulary.permitted_later_resolution: A later authorized observation may become available, but the earlier denial remains evidence.
controlled_vocabulary.required_evidence: An explicit denial, authorization requirement, or equivalent access-control outcome.

canonical_case_example.description: The provider timeline contains an explicit PR-head-ref deletion lifecycle event.

controlled_vocabulary.meaning: Explicit provider evidence reports deletion or a tombstone.
controlled_vocabulary.permitted_later_resolution: A later restoration is a new lifecycle observation and does not erase the deletion event.
controlled_vocabulary.required_evidence: An explicit provider deletion event or tombstone bound to the subject.

canonical_case_example.description: The original repository identity behind the deleted PR head ref cannot be established.

controlled_vocabulary.meaning: Available evidence cannot establish the value or state.
controlled_vocabulary.permitted_later_resolution: New evidence may resolve the value through a new observation or accepted correction; the prior unknown remains historical.
controlled_vocabulary.required_evidence: A bounded evidence review showing that available evidence cannot establish the value.

canonical_case_example.description: The single case does not support a universal transfer conclusion.

controlled_vocabulary.meaning: The current contract or provider surface intentionally cannot represent or support the concept.
controlled_vocabulary.permitted_later_resolution: A later version or additional canonical case may add support, while the earlier contract remains unsupported.
controlled_vocabulary.required_evidence: An explicit contract boundary or reviewed support determination.

canonical_case_example.description: No unresolved conflict is present: recorded base and merge first parent differ because they have distinct roles and were reconciled explicitly.

controlled_vocabulary.meaning: Two or more evidence-bearing observations disagree and no accepted resolution exists.
controlled_vocabulary.permitted_later_resolution: Only a later accepted decision or correction may resolve it, preserving all conflicting evidence and the resolution history.
controlled_vocabulary.required_evidence: At least two identified disagreeing observations with equivalent semantic roles and no accepted resolution.

decision.rationale: The evidence distinguishes observed null, missing, unavailable, deleted, unknown, and unsupported states; inaccessible and conflict must remain independently available without being fabricated in this case.
decision.title: Explicit field-state semantics

decision.rationale: ArtifactSnapshot is a legacy Issue-bound UTF-8 JSON-text retrieval observation, not a stable source-identity carrier; S08 alone owns its compatibility fate.
decision.title: Limited ArtifactSnapshot boundary

decision.rationale: Object or bounded-surface location does not encode chronology, meaning, causality, review, selection, or other relationship semantics.
decision.title: Discussion and relationship-surface boundary

decision.rationale: The current Issue-only internal model is retained unchanged; its alias field and ambiguous numeric object_id cannot acquire new stable-identity meaning retroactively.
decision.title: Legacy SourceLocator disposition

decision.rationale: Stable repository plus immutable revision plus exact path identifies a file; bounded coordinates belong to a separate S1.P02 locator contract and not legacy SourceLocator.
decision.title: Revision-qualified path and locator boundary

decision.rationale: Identity, request, response, acquisition, artifact, transformation, correction, interpretation, and publication facts have different authorities and timestamps and must never overwrite one another.
decision.title: Source identity and provenance layers

layers.authority: Product authority plus bounded provider observations
layers.correction_or_supersession_behavior: A correction may add or supersede an authority observation without rewriting prior declarations.
layers.forbidden_overwrite: Must not be overwritten by a retrieval host, URL, or later representation.
layers.identity_ownership: Provider key and authority role only
layers.subject: Source provider and named navigation or retrieval authorities
layers.timestamp_ownership: Authority declarations own no provider event timestamp; authority observations own their observation time.

layers.correction_or_supersession_behavior: Corrections add evidence or resolve conflict; rename and transfer add alias observations.
layers.forbidden_overwrite: A mutable alias, URL, ref, or retrieval route cannot replace stable repository identity.
layers.identity_ownership: Provider plus provider stable repository ID
layers.subject: Stable repository identity
layers.timestamp_ownership: Stable identity owns no alias-observation timestamp.

layers.authority: Provider identity surface under stable repository scope where applicable
layers.correction_or_supersession_behavior: Corrections may link alternate identifiers or resolve conflicts while preserving original observations.
layers.forbidden_overwrite: Alternate IDs, logins, parent relationships, and URLs cannot overwrite the primary typed identity.
layers.identity_ownership: Object kind plus kind-appropriate scoped or global stable identifiers
layers.subject: Repository, Issue, PR, comment, review, timeline, and attribution objects
layers.timestamp_ownership: Provider object event timestamps and identity observations remain distinct fields.

layers.authority: Git object model for commits, trees, and blobs; FaultAtlas hashing for retained artifacts
layers.correction_or_supersession_behavior: A correction may amend metadata or supersede an artifact record, never mutate the identified bytes.
layers.forbidden_overwrite: A role, ref, path, artifact SHA-256, or later acquisition cannot replace Git object identity.
layers.identity_ownership: Kind- and algorithm-qualified Git digest or artifact digest plus declared digest scope
layers.subject: Git object or immutable exact artifact identity
layers.timestamp_ownership: Commit times and artifact acquisition times do not form part of immutable digest identity.

layers.authority: Observed provider or repository state under an authority
layers.correction_or_supersession_behavior: Later rename, transfer, retarget, or deletion creates another observation; no prior observation is rewritten.
layers.forbidden_overwrite: The observation cannot become stable repository or immutable revision identity.
layers.identity_ownership: Repository identity plus alias/ref name, observed target, state, authority, and time
layers.subject: Repository alias or mutable Git ref at one observation
layers.timestamp_ownership: The observation time belongs to the alias or ref observation.

layers.authority: FaultAtlas acquisition procedure and requesting client
layers.correction_or_supersession_behavior: Retries and supplemental requests are new request records and remain time-accurate.
layers.forbidden_overwrite: Request URL, host, API version, media, and HTTP controls cannot overwrite source identity.
layers.identity_ownership: Request ordinal, authority, route, controls, media request, and procedure identity
layers.subject: One bounded request attempt
layers.timestamp_ownership: Request-start time belongs here, not to the provider object.

layers.authority: Retrieval authority response plus FaultAtlas verification
layers.correction_or_supersession_behavior: A later representation is another observation; corrections link rather than overwrite it.
layers.forbidden_overwrite: Normalized values cannot be labeled raw bytes, and response time cannot become provider event time.
layers.identity_ownership: Representation media, availability, byte classification, and response/request linkage
layers.subject: Response metadata and the observed representation
layers.timestamp_ownership: Response completion and observation time belong here; provider events retain their own timestamps.

layers.correction_or_supersession_behavior: An append-only correction may describe a run nonconformance without rewriting the run bytes.
layers.forbidden_overwrite: A later supplemental observation cannot be backdated into the original run.
layers.identity_ownership: Run ID, procedure, baseline, status, and request/observation membership
layers.subject: Governed acquisition run
layers.timestamp_ownership: Run start and seal times belong to the run and do not date provider events.

layers.correction_or_supersession_behavior: A corrected descriptor or replacement artifact is additive and explicitly linked.
layers.forbidden_overwrite: Transformation or normalization cannot overwrite exact retained bytes or their digest.
layers.identity_ownership: Artifact path, byte length, media, digest algorithm/scope/value, and source/revision linkage
layers.subject: Exact bytes retained by FaultAtlas
layers.timestamp_ownership: Retention/acquisition time belongs to the artifact record, not to source creation.

layers.correction_or_supersession_behavior: A correction may supersede transformation metadata while preserving input, output, and earlier record.
layers.forbidden_overwrite: Derived or normalized output cannot be relabeled as raw provider bytes or overwrite input.
layers.identity_ownership: Input/output identities, procedure/version, operation, and digest relationship
layers.subject: Derivation from one representation or artifact to another
layers.timestamp_ownership: Transformation time belongs only to the transformation event.

layers.correction_or_supersession_behavior: Further corrections append and explicitly reference the record or decision they resolve.
layers.forbidden_overwrite: A correction cannot erase the historical existence or exact bytes of its target.
layers.identity_ownership: Correction ID, immutable target lock, findings, resolution, and supersession semantics
layers.subject: Semantic correction or supersession of a specific durable record
layers.timestamp_ownership: Correction creation and seal times belong to the correction, not the target acquisition.

layers.correction_or_supersession_behavior: Supersession adds a new manifest/correction and preserves the published manifest.
layers.forbidden_overwrite: A manifest relationship cannot overwrite source identity, chronology, or provider facts.
layers.identity_ownership: Case-local entity IDs, relationship classifications, predicates, and evidence pointers
layers.subject: Case entity and relationship assertions over locked evidence
layers.timestamp_ownership: Case publication timestamps belong to the manifest; cited provider events retain their own times.

layers.correction_or_supersession_behavior: Later review may supersede an interpretation while preserving the prior version and cited evidence.
layers.forbidden_overwrite: An interpretation cannot become raw evidence, provider-authored meaning, or established causation without evidence.
layers.identity_ownership: Interpretation ID, producer/reviewer, review state, and immutable evidence references
layers.subject: Reviewed selection, technical role, invariant, or other interpretation
layers.timestamp_ownership: Interpretation creation/review time belongs to the interpretation, never to source events.

layers.authority: FaultAtlas repository and protected review/merge process
layers.correction_or_supersession_behavior: A later publication or supersession references and preserves earlier published artifacts.
layers.forbidden_overwrite: Publication metadata cannot backdate source, response, acquisition, correction, or interpretation events.
layers.identity_ownership: Published path, content digest, commit/tree, review, merge, and release identities where available
layers.subject: Publication of a FaultAtlas artifact
layers.timestamp_ownership: Commit, PR, merge, and release times belong to publication only.

decision.rationale: The provider-assigned repository ID survives mutable aliases; the case does not establish the deleted head repository identity.
decision.title: Stable repository identity and alias observations

decision.rationale: Kind and algorithm qualify immutable Git object identity, while case roles and mutable ref observations remain separate evidence-bearing records.
decision.title: Git object, revision role, and ref observation

owner_decisions.compatibility_consequence: Legacy SourceLocator remains alias-bound and its object_id remains ambiguous; future consumers require typed identity or an explicit compatibility mapping.
owner_decisions.question: How should provider, stable repository identity, timed aliases, object kind, repository-scoped numbers, global REST IDs, and GraphQL node IDs compose without ambiguity?
owner_decisions.rationale: The default is accepted and refined into separate provider, repository, alias, object-kind, scoped-number, REST-ID, and node-ID roles.

owner_decisions.compatibility_consequence: Current generic limitation fields are not repurposed as actor or reviewer identity state; future identity carriers must map states explicitly.
owner_decisions.question: How should actor and reviewer identities distinguish observed values, observed null, omitted, unavailable, inaccessible, and unknown?
owner_decisions.rationale: The default is accepted and refined to the nine-state vocabulary, including missing, deleted, unsupported, and conflict without fabricating states not observed in this case.

owner_decisions.compatibility_consequence: Artifact SHA-256 values and Git SHA-1 object identities remain typed and scope-qualified rather than sharing a generic digest string.
owner_decisions.question: How should commits, trees, blobs, comparison endpoints, and their hash algorithms be explicitly identified?
owner_decisions.rationale: The kind-specific default is accepted and refined to require object kind, algorithm, and full digest while leaving class names and wire syntax unchosen.

owner_decisions.compatibility_consequence: Legacy SourceLocator is not expanded; ordered topology, ref lifecycle, revision-qualified paths, and bounded coordinates require separate future contracts.
owner_decisions.question: How should ordered parents, distinct base and first-parent roles, mutable or deleted refs, revision-qualified paths, and line, byte, and hunk ranges compose?
owner_decisions.rationale: The composable default is accepted at the conceptual boundary; concrete locator syntax, coordinate indexing, and implementation remain deferred to S1.P02.

owner_decisions.compatibility_consequence: SourceLocator.provider and ArtifactSnapshot.retrieved_at are not expanded or reinterpreted as complete authority or provenance records.
owner_decisions.question: How should navigation authority, retrieval API authority, request provenance, URL construction provenance, observation time, and publication provenance compose?
owner_decisions.rationale: The typed-record default is accepted and refined into fourteen non-overwriting layers with separately owned timestamps and identities.

decision.rationale: Repository-scoped numbers, REST global IDs, GraphQL node IDs, object kinds, and parent scope carry different identity semantics and cannot share one ambiguous field.
decision.title: Typed provider object identity roles

terms.definition: A stable key for the source ecosystem; github in this case.
A named origin or governing source for a fact or reference.
The human-facing authority used to derive navigation references; github.com here.
The machine authority from which a representation is requested; api.github.com here.
Provider identity plus provider-assigned stable repository ID.
An authority-qualified and time-qualified observation of a mutable repository owner/name alias.
An object number whose meaning depends on stable repository identity and object kind.
A provider-assigned object identifier whose scope differs from a repository-scoped number.
A typed alternate provider identifier observed from a GraphQL-compatible provider surface.
Provider, stable repository where applicable, object kind, and the kind-appropriate stable identifier components.
Object kind, hash algorithm, and full digest for a commit, tree, or blob.
An algorithm-qualified immutable commit identity, distinct from any mutable ref or case role.
A case-relative role such as base, head, merge first parent, or merge assigned to a commit identity.
A repository-, name-, time-, target-, and lifecycle-qualified observation of a mutable Git ref.
Stable repository identity, immutable revision identity, exact repository-relative path, and explicit path rules.
A separate S1.P02-owned coordinate record bound to a parent artifact or revision-qualified file.
A representation or state seen at an explicit observation time under a stated authority.
A governed run that makes retrievals, records observations, and retains bounded artifacts.
Exact retained bytes with media, digest scope, digest, and acquisition provenance.
A deterministic derived representation that is not raw provider bytes.
A separately recorded operation that derives a new representation without rewriting its input.
An append-only semantic supplement or supersession that preserves the historical target record.
A reviewed case-level conclusion that cites evidence and remains distinct from source fact.
FaultAtlas commit, review, merge, and release facts for a published internal artifact.
Concrete encoding and coordinate-index syntax remain provisional until S1.P02.
Mapping these conceptual boundaries to providers beyond GitHub remains provisional pending canonical cases.
The original repository identity behind the deleted PR head ref is not established by retained evidence.
